# Bosun's data model

<!-- Generated by `uv run bosun db --doc`. Do not edit: change src/bosun/datamodel.py or the schema comments in src/bosun/migrations.py, then regenerate. -->

Schema v15. Everything Bosun knows is in one SQLite file, `bosun.db`, in its data folder (`uv run bosun db` prints the path).

## Asking it a question

```
uv run bosun query "SELECT item_key, lane, risk FROM v_current_items ORDER BY risk DESC"
uv run bosun query --json "SELECT * FROM v_failures"   # columns and rows as JSON
uv run bosun query --schema                              # what can be read
```

The dashboard answers the same at `GET /api/query?sql=...` (the `query` action).

A query is one `SELECT`. It runs on a read-only connection, may read only the views and tables below, returns at most 500 rows (`--limit`, up to 5000) and is stopped after 2 seconds. Writes, `ATTACH`, `PRAGMA` and a second statement are refused. Times are Unix seconds: `datetime(ts, 'unixepoch', 'localtime')` makes them readable. JSON columns unpack with `json_extract` and `json_each`.

Start with the views. They are the contract: their columns stay, whatever happens to the tables under them.

## Views

| View | Answers |
|---|---|
| `v_current_items` | What is outdated or vulnerable right now: one row per item in the latest snapshot, with its lane, risk and why. The same items the dashboard shows. |
| `v_item_history` | What happened to each item over time: one row when it appeared, each time its lane, versions or risk changed, and when it was gone. Snapshots where nothing changed have no row. Filter on item_key: one item's history is an index lookup, the whole table is a scan of a year of rows. |
| `v_open_vulns` | Every vulnerability open right now, one row per vulnerability per item it touches, with the project and how long it has been open there. |
| `v_failures` | What failed: upgrade, pin and relaunch jobs, Branch + test fixes, and any other run that failed, was partial or was interrupted. Each failure appears once: as its job or fix when it has one, otherwise as its run. With the error and the last command that failed in it. |
| `v_triage` | One triage verdict per failed job, fix or run, with the unpacked cause, confidence and suggested next step. |
| `v_llm_spend` | What Claude cost: calls, tokens and list-price cost per day, purpose, model and item. |
| `v_ai_spend` | AI calls per day, provider, login, job and model: calls, tokens, window draw and list-price cost. |
| `v_actions` | The audit trail: every action that changed something, who asked for it, through which surface, with what input and how it ended. Reads are not recorded. Input that fails validation never becomes an action, so it is not here either. |
| `v_automations` | Owner-written automation rules: trigger, conditions, action, scope, mode, limits and 90-day INSTALL grant expiry. |
| `v_automation_firings` | History of every automation firing: matching event, status, resolved input, linked action run and offer decision. |

### v_current_items

What is outdated or vulnerable right now: one row per item in the latest snapshot, with its lane, risk and why. The same items the dashboard shows.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `item_key` | Stable id, e.g. `brew:jq` or `repo:npm:lodash@<project>`. Every action takes these. |
| `name` |  |
| `source` | brew, winget, apt, repo, container, image, secret, mcp, macos... |
| `scope` | machine, or project (fixed by editing a project's files) |
| `project` | project key (git remote URL or path); '' for machine items |
| `project_name` |  |
| `kind` | os, firmware, driver, hardware, browser, app, component, dev, project |
| `package_id` |  |
| `ecosystem` | OSV ecosystem (npm, PyPI...) when there is one |
| `installed` |  |
| `available` | NULL = nothing to upgrade to |
| `lane` | now, plan, watch, batch, later, dormant: what to do about it. |
| `readiness` | ready, work, blocked |
| `risk` | 0-10. 10 = actively exploited; otherwise the worst relevant CVSS. |
| `tier` | critical, high, medium, low |
| `score` |  |
| `kev` | 1 = a vulnerability here is in CISA's Known Exploited list |
| `malicious` | 1 = the package itself is reported as malware |
| `max_cvss` | worst CVSS among the vulnerabilities upgrading fixes |
| `max_epss` | highest EPSS (chance of exploitation in 30 days) |
| `reach` | how the worst vulnerability is reached (network, local...) |
| `vulns_fixed` | vulnerabilities that upgrading to `available` fixes |
| `vulns_remaining` | vulnerabilities still there after upgrading |
| `unsupported` | 1 = past end of life |
| `ends_soon` | 1 = end of life within about 6 months |
| `support_ends` | ISO date security fixes stop |
| `upgradable` | 1 = Bosun can run the upgrade itself |
| `ignored` | 1 = you ignored it, or its whole project. Follows the dashboard as soon as you change it. |
| `auto_upgrade` | 1 = opted into automatic upgrades |
| `migration_effort` | none, low, high; '' = not assessed |
| `upgrade_value` | critical, high, medium, low, skip |
| `headline` | one line on what the upgrade brings |
| `reasons` | JSON list of why it scored as it did. Unpack with `json_each(reasons)`. |
| `first_seen` | Unix time this item was first recorded. |
| `days_open` | Days since first_seen. |
| `snapshot_id` |  |
| `snapshot_ts` | When the snapshot was taken: how fresh this answer is. |

```sql
SELECT item_key, installed, available, lane, risk, headline FROM v_current_items WHERE lane = 'now' AND NOT ignored ORDER BY risk DESC
```

### v_item_history

What happened to each item over time: one row when it appeared, each time its lane, versions or risk changed, and when it was gone. Snapshots where nothing changed have no row. Filter on item_key: one item's history is an index lookup, the whole table is a scan of a year of rows.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `item_key` | stable across snapshots, e.g. brew:jq or repo:npm:lodash@<project> |
| `name` |  |
| `source` | brew, winget, apt, repo, container, image, secret, mcp, macos... |
| `project` | project key (git remote URL or path); '' for machine items |
| `snapshot_id` | The snapshot the event belongs to. For gone: the first snapshot without the item. |
| `ts` |  |
| `event` | appeared (first time recorded), reappeared (after being gone), changed, or gone. Gone means it was not in that snapshot: upgraded, removed, or its collector failed that day. |
| `lane_before` | Lane in the snapshot before, for changed and gone. The other *_before columns likewise. |
| `lane` | Lane from this snapshot on. NULL for gone, as are installed, available and risk. |
| `installed_before` |  |
| `installed` |  |
| `available_before` |  |
| `available` | NULL = nothing to upgrade to |
| `risk_before` |  |
| `risk` | 0-10: 10 = actively exploited, else the worst relevant CVSS |

```sql
SELECT datetime(ts, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS at, event, lane_before, lane, installed, available FROM v_item_history WHERE item_key = 'brew:jq' ORDER BY snapshot_id
```

### v_open_vulns

Every vulnerability open right now, one row per vulnerability per item it touches, with the project and how long it has been open there.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `vuln_id` | As the advisory names it (GHSA-, CVE-, MAL-); `cve` has the CVE id when there is one. |
| `cve` |  |
| `summary` |  |
| `cvss` |  |
| `epss` |  |
| `epss_pct` |  |
| `kev` | 1 = a vulnerability here is in CISA's Known Exploited list |
| `malicious` | 1 = the package itself is reported as malware |
| `url` |  |
| `item_key` | stable across snapshots, e.g. brew:jq or repo:npm:lodash@<project> |
| `name` |  |
| `source` | brew, winget, apt, repo, container, image, secret, mcp, macos... |
| `project` | project key (git remote URL or path); '' for machine items |
| `project_name` |  |
| `installed` |  |
| `available` | NULL = nothing to upgrade to |
| `lane` | now, plan, watch, batch, later, dormant |
| `ignored` | 1 = you ignored the item or its whole project |
| `fixed_by_upgrade` | 1 = upgrading the item to `available` fixes it; 0 = it remains after upgrading. |
| `first_seen` | Unix time this vulnerability was first recorded on this item. |
| `days_open` | Days since first_seen. |

```sql
SELECT vuln_id, cvss, kev, COUNT(*) AS items, MAX(days_open) AS longest_open FROM v_open_vulns GROUP BY vuln_id ORDER BY kev DESC, cvss DESC
```

### v_failures

What failed: upgrade, pin and relaunch jobs, Branch + test fixes, and any other run that failed, was partial or was interrupted. Each failure appears once: as its job or fix when it has one, otherwise as its run. With the error and the last command that failed in it.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `what` | job, fix or run. |
| `id` | The job id, fix id, or the run's trace id (as text). |
| `kind` | The run's kind: refresh, recheck, upgrade, pin, relaunch, fix, action... |
| `subject` | The item key for a job or fix; what the run was about otherwise. |
| `status` |  |
| `ts` |  |
| `actor` |  |
| `error` |  |
| `trace_id` | Pass it to `bosun trace` or the get_trace and diagnose actions for the whole timeline. |
| `failed_command` | JSON list: the argv of the last command that failed in that run (secrets masked). |
| `failed_exit` | Its exit code. |
| `failed_output` | The tail of its stderr, or of its stdout when stderr was empty. Kept for 30 days. |

```sql
SELECT datetime(ts, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS at, what, kind, subject, error, failed_command FROM v_failures ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 20
```

### v_triage

One triage verdict per failed job, fix or run, with the unpacked cause, confidence and suggested next step.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` |  |
| `failure` | job:<id>, fix:<id> or run:<trace_id>; unique. |
| `trace_id` | The failed run's trace id. |
| `signature` | SHA-256 over the normalized failure kind, source, command verb, exit code and error line. |
| `status` | queued, running, waiting_quota, done, skipped, failed or fixed_since. |
| `source` | rules, cache or model. |
| `same_as` | For cache rows: the origin triage.id whose verdict this reuses. |
| `triage_trace` | The model triage run's own trace id, if a model ran. |
| `feedback` | helpful, wrong, disputed, or empty. |
| `feedback_ts` |  |
| `created` |  |
| `finished` |  |
| `category` | One of the 16 verdict categories (permissions, busy_or_locked, network, ...). |
| `cause` | One-sentence explanation of why the run failed. |
| `confidence` | high, medium or low. |
| `next_step_kind` | recipe, retry, rescan, runbook, agent_prompt or none. |
| `next_step_recipe` | Terminal recipe name when next_step_kind is recipe. |
| `next_step_runbook` | Runbook topic under docs/runbooks/ when next_step_kind is runbook. |
| `next_step_why` | One sentence explaining the suggested next step. |
| `needs_person` | 1 = retrying unattended would fail the same way. |
| `transient` | 1 = likely to succeed on a later try with no change. |

```sql
SELECT datetime(created, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS at, failure, source, category, cause, next_step_kind FROM v_triage WHERE status = 'done' ORDER BY created DESC LIMIT 20
```

### v_llm_spend

What Claude cost: calls, tokens and list-price cost per day, purpose, model and item.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `day` | Local date. |
| `purpose` |  |
| `model` | What Bosun asked for (an alias like haiku, or a full id). |
| `item_key` |  |
| `project` |  |
| `calls` | Calls that reached Claude (or tried to). |
| `cached` | Calls Bosun's own cache made unnecessary. |
| `skipped` | Calls not made: nothing to summarize (older rows: a retired dollar budget was spent). |
| `cost_usd` |  |
| `input_tokens` |  |
| `output_tokens` |  |
| `cache_read_tokens` |  |
| `cache_write_tokens` |  |

```sql
SELECT day, purpose, SUM(calls) AS calls, ROUND(SUM(cost_usd), 2) AS usd FROM v_llm_spend GROUP BY day, purpose ORDER BY day DESC
```

### v_ai_spend

AI calls per day, provider, login, job and model: calls, tokens, window draw and list-price cost.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `day` | Local date. |
| `provider` | Which CLI ran: claude, codex, gemini, grok, antigravity, muse. |
| `account` | Which login ran: default or an added login's id. |
| `job` | summarize, explain, triage, fix, assistant, computer_use. |
| `model` | What Bosun asked for (an alias or full id). |
| `calls` | Calls that reached the CLI (or tried to). |
| `cached` | Calls Bosun's own cache made unnecessary. |
| `skipped` | Calls not made: there was nothing to summarize. |
| `tokens` | Total tokens (input, output, cache reads and cache writes). |
| `window_draw` | Sum of usage-window share rises attributed to these calls, where reported. |
| `estimated` | Calls whose CLI reports no usage windows (use counted from calls and tokens). |
| `cost_usd` | List-price cost where the CLI reports it, kept as detail. |

```sql
SELECT day, provider, account, job, SUM(calls) AS calls, SUM(tokens) AS tokens FROM v_ai_spend GROUP BY day, provider, account, job ORDER BY day DESC
```

### v_actions

The audit trail: every action that changed something, who asked for it, through which surface, with what input and how it ended. Reads are not recorded. Input that fails validation never becomes an action, so it is not here either.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` |  |
| `ts` |  |
| `actor` | user, autopilot, schedule, assistant, or agent:<name>. |
| `action` |  |
| `risk` |  |
| `surface` | http (the dashboard), cli, mcp, assistant. |
| `input` | JSON, secrets masked. |
| `outcome` | ok or error; `error` then has the error's class and message. |
| `error` |  |
| `duration_ms` |  |
| `trace_id` |  |
| `runs_started` | Runs this action started (the upgrade it queued, the refresh it began). |

```sql
SELECT datetime(ts, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS at, actor, action, input, outcome, error FROM v_actions ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 20
```

### v_automations

Owner-written automation rules: trigger, conditions, action, scope, mode, limits and 90-day INSTALL grant expiry.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` |  |
| `name` |  |
| `preset` |  |
| `enabled` | 1 = active, 0 = off. |
| `paused_reason` | Non-empty when paused by the circuit breaker after consecutive failures. |
| `trigger` |  |
| `conditions` |  |
| `action` |  |
| `scope` |  |
| `mode` | run (runs on its own) or ask (asks first). |
| `delay_s` |  |
| `max_per_day` |  |
| `cooldown_s` |  |
| `model_jobs_per_day` |  |
| `grant_digest` |  |
| `granted_by` |  |
| `granted_at` |  |
| `grant_expires_at` | Unix time a runs-on-its-own INSTALL grant expires (granted_at + 90 days); NULL for LOCAL, notify or ask. |

| `updated` |  |

```sql
SELECT id, name, action, mode, enabled, paused_reason, grant_expires_at FROM v_automations ORDER BY id
```

### v_automation_firings

History of every automation firing: matching event, status, resolved input, linked action run and offer decision.

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` |  |
| `automation_id` |  |
| `automation_name` | Copied when created so history survives rule deletion. |
| `event_kind` |  |
| `event_ref` |  |
| `dedup_key` | Unique per automation_id to prevent double runs. |
| `depth` |  |
| `status` | scheduled, waiting_quota, offered, running, done, failed, skipped, missed, declined, expired or refused. |
| `due` |  |
| `deadline` |  |
| `input` |  |
| `trace_id` | Action run trace_id started by this firing, if any. |
| `reason` |  |
| `decided_by` | Who approved or declined an offer (`user`), or empty. |
| `decided` |  |
| `started_at` |  |
| `created` |  |
| `finished` |  |

```sql
SELECT datetime(created, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS at, automation_name, event_kind, status, reason FROM v_automation_firings ORDER BY created DESC LIMIT 20
```

## Tables

The views are built from these. They can be read directly when a view doesn't answer the question.

### snapshot_log

One row per snapshot (a refresh or a re-check). Kept for a year; after a month, only the last of each day.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot_id` | INTEGER | snapshots.id; this row stays after the blob is dropped |
| `ts` | REAL | when the snapshot was saved |
| `items` | INTEGER | rows written to snapshot_items |
| `errors` | INTEGER | collectors and steps that failed in that refresh |
| `backfilled` | INTEGER | 1 = rebuilt from a stored blob by migration v4, not written at save time |

### snapshot_items

One row per item per snapshot: the history behind v_current_items and v_item_history. Kept for a year.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot_id` | INTEGER | snapshot_log.snapshot_id. |
| `item_key` | TEXT | stable across snapshots, e.g. brew:jq or repo:npm:lodash@<project> |
| `source` | TEXT | brew, winget, apt, repo, container, image, secret, mcp, macos... |
| `scope` | TEXT | machine, or project (fixed by editing a project's files) |
| `project` | TEXT | project key (git remote URL or path); '' for machine items |
| `project_name` | TEXT |  |
| `name` | TEXT |  |
| `package_id` | TEXT |  |
| `ecosystem` | TEXT | OSV ecosystem (npm, PyPI...) when there is one |
| `kind` | TEXT | os, firmware, driver, hardware, browser, app, component, dev, project |
| `installed` | TEXT |  |
| `available` | TEXT | NULL = nothing to upgrade to |
| `lane` | TEXT | now, plan, watch, batch, later, dormant |
| `readiness` | TEXT | ready, work, blocked |
| `tier` | TEXT | critical, high, medium, low |
| `score` | INTEGER |  |
| `risk` | REAL | 0-10: 10 = actively exploited, else the worst relevant CVSS |
| `kev` | INTEGER | 1 = a vulnerability here is in CISA's Known Exploited list |
| `malicious` | INTEGER | 1 = the package itself is reported as malware |
| `max_cvss` | REAL | worst CVSS among the vulnerabilities upgrading fixes |
| `max_epss` | REAL | highest EPSS (chance of exploitation in 30 days) |
| `reach` | TEXT | how the worst vulnerability is reached (network, local...) |
| `vulns_fixed` | INTEGER | vulnerabilities that upgrading to `available` fixes |
| `vulns_remaining` | INTEGER | vulnerabilities still there after upgrading |
| `unsupported` | INTEGER | 1 = past end of life |
| `ends_soon` | INTEGER | 1 = end of life within about 6 months |
| `support_ends` | TEXT | ISO date security fixes stop |
| `upgradable` | INTEGER | 1 = Bosun can run the upgrade itself |
| `ignored` | INTEGER | 1 = you ignored the item or its whole project |
| `auto_upgrade` | INTEGER | 1 = opted into automatic upgrades |
| `migration_effort` | TEXT | none, low, high; '' = not assessed |
| `upgrade_value` | TEXT | critical, high, medium, low, skip |
| `headline` | TEXT | one line on what the upgrade brings |
| `reasons` | TEXT | JSON list: why it scored as it did |
| `first_seen` | REAL | when this item was first recorded (survives pruning) |
| `first_seen_snapshot` | INTEGER | The snapshot it was first recorded in. |
| `state` | TEXT | '' = open (in front of you); ack, snoozed or ignored = put away, as of that snapshot. The latest snapshot follows the dashboard as soon as you change it. `item_states` has since when and until when. |

### item_states

What you said about an item without updating it: acknowledged, snoozed or ignored. No row = open. An item comes back by itself when it gets riskier (attention.py), so join `snapshot_items.state` for what is in front of you now.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `item_key` | TEXT | the item you put away (never a project) |
| `state` | TEXT | ack (seen, not acting now), snoozed (until a date or the next version), ignored |
| `state_at` | REAL | when you said so |
| `until_ts` | REAL | snoozed until a date: when it comes back |
| `until_version` | TEXT | snoozed as "skip this version": the version skipped; another one brings it back |
| `seen_risk` | REAL | its risk when you said so: it comes back when risk reaches 7 from below |
| `seen_kev` | INTEGER | 1 = it was already known to be exploited then |
| `seen_malicious` | INTEGER | 1 = it was already reported as malware then |

### vulns

One row per vulnerability Bosun has seen, with its latest details.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT | as the advisory source names it: GHSA-..., CVE-..., MAL-... |
| `cve` | TEXT | its CVE id, when it has one |
| `aliases` | TEXT | JSON list of its other ids |
| `summary` | TEXT |  |
| `cvss` | REAL |  |
| `vector` | TEXT | CVSS vector string |
| `epss` | REAL | chance of exploitation in the next 30 days (FIRST EPSS) |
| `epss_pct` | REAL | EPSS percentile among all CVEs |
| `kev` | INTEGER | 1 = in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list |
| `malicious` | INTEGER | 1 = a malicious-package report (MAL-...) |
| `url` | TEXT |  |
| `first_seen` | REAL | first snapshot it appeared in, on any item |
| `last_seen` | REAL | latest snapshot it appeared in; details are as of then |

### item_vulns

Which vulnerability touched which item in which snapshot. Kept for a year.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot_id` | INTEGER |  |
| `item_key` | TEXT |  |
| `vuln_id` | TEXT | vulns.id. |
| `fixed` | INTEGER | 1 = upgrading to the item's `available` fixes it; 0 = it remains |
| `first_seen` | REAL | when this vulnerability was first recorded on this item |

| `id` | INTEGER |  |
| `ts` | REAL |  |
| `actor` | TEXT | user, autopilot, schedule, assistant, agent:<name> |
| `action` | TEXT | the registry action's name |

One row per unit of work (a refresh, an upgrade, a fix, an action). Kept for a year.

### quota_windows

The latest reading of each plan usage window (5-hour, weekly, per model) per AI login. A reading past `resets_at`, or undated and a week old, says nothing about now.

| `bucket` | TEXT | a login: claude, or claude@work for an added one |

| `status` | TEXT | allowed, allowed_warning, rejected |
| `used` | REAL | share used, 0 to 1; NULL = the CLI gave no figure (unknown, not 0%) |
| `resets_at` | REAL | when it resets (epoch seconds); NULL = not said |
| `at` | REAL | when it was read |
| `source` | TEXT | output (a call's own output), probe, coho, limit |

### triage

One error-triage verdict per failed job, fix or run: cause, confidence, evidence and suggested next step. Kept for a year.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | INTEGER | stable row id referenced by cached copies (same_as) |
| `failure` | TEXT | job:<id>, fix:<id>, or run:<trace_id>; one row per failure |
| `trace_id` | TEXT | the failed run's trace_id |
| `signature` | TEXT | SHA-256 over normalized failure kind, source, verb, exit code and error line |
| `status` | TEXT | queued, running, waiting_quota, done, skipped, failed, fixed_since |
| `source` | TEXT | rules, cache, model, or '' before completion |
| `verdict` | TEXT | checked and redacted Verdict JSON, or '' when none |
| `same_as` | INTEGER | for cache rows: the origin triage.id whose verdict was reused |
| `triage_trace` | TEXT | the model triage job's own trace_id, if a model ran |
| `feedback` | TEXT | helpful, wrong, disputed, or '' |
| `feedback_ts` | REAL | Unix time feedback was last updated |
| `created` | REAL | Unix time this triage row was created |
| `finished` | REAL | Unix time triage reached a terminal status |
| `last_error` | TEXT | Redacted error from the latest failed model triage attempt (empty when none). |

### triage_disputed_rules

Failure signatures whose deterministic rules verdict the user marked wrong, so later runs skip that rule even after a model triage attempt.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `signature` | TEXT | SHA-256 failure signature whose deterministic rule was marked wrong |
| `disputed_at` | REAL | Unix time the rule was disputed |

### automations

Owner-written automation rules (trigger, conditions, action, scope, grant and limits).

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | INTEGER | stable row id for this automation |
| `name` | TEXT | owner-chosen display name |
| `preset` | TEXT | shipped preset id, or NULL for custom rules |
| `enabled` | INTEGER | 1 = active, 0 = off |
| `paused_reason` | TEXT | set by the circuit breaker when paused after consecutive failures |
| `trigger` | TEXT | validated trigger JSON |
| `conditions` | TEXT | validated conditions JSON |
| `action` | TEXT | allow-listed action name (or notify) |
| `scope` | TEXT | validated scope JSON |
| `mode` | TEXT | run (runs on its own) or ask (asks first) |
| `delay_s` | INTEGER | seconds to wait between event and execution |
| `max_per_day` | INTEGER | daily firing limit for this rule (1-48) |
| `cooldown_s` | INTEGER | minimum seconds between firings of this rule |
| `model_jobs_per_day` | INTEGER | daily cap on AI model jobs started by this rule |
| `grant_digest` | TEXT | SHA-256 of the definition granted at save time |
| `granted_by` | TEXT | who granted this automation (user) |
| `granted_at` | REAL | Unix time the current grant was saved or renewed |
| `created` | REAL | Unix time this automation was created |
| `updated` | REAL | Unix time this automation was last updated |

### automation_firings

One row per event that matched an automation, with status, resolved input, trace_id and reason. Terminal rows are kept for a year.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | INTEGER | stable firing id |
| `automation_id` | INTEGER | automations.id (history survives delete) |
| `automation_name` | TEXT | copied automation name so history survives delete |
| `event_kind` | TEXT | refresh, schedule, verdict, or in_app_update |
| `event_ref` | TEXT | event subject (snap:<id>, slot key, failure id, app@ver) |
| `dedup_key` | TEXT | unique per automation_id to stop double runs |
| `depth` | INTEGER | chain depth (0 = external event, 1 = from a depth-0 automation) |
| `status` | TEXT | scheduled, waiting_quota, offered, running, done, failed, skipped, missed, declined, expired, refused |
| `due` | REAL | Unix time this firing is due to run |
| `deadline` | REAL | Unix time after which waiting_quota skips or offered expires |
| `input` | TEXT | redacted resolved action input JSON |
| `trace_id` | TEXT | trace_id of the action run started by this firing |
| `reason` | TEXT | redacted plain-text reason for skip, refusal, failure or digest line |
| `decided_by` | TEXT | who approved or declined an offer (user) |
| `decided` | REAL | Unix time an offer was approved or declined |
| `started_at` | REAL | Unix time the action call began (NULL before action call) |
| `created` | REAL | Unix time this firing row was created |
| `finished` | REAL | Unix time this firing reached a terminal status |

## Not readable

`settings`, `cache`, `prefs`, `offers` and legacy `peers` hold Bosun's own configuration, cached API answers and internal state; `query` refuses them, along with SQLite's own tables (`sqlite_master`). An item's ignore and auto-upgrade preferences are in `v_current_items`; what you acknowledged or snoozed is in `item_states` and `snapshot_items.state`. The session key is a file, not in the database.
